title: Industrial DataGraph
summary: A microcontroller-based sensor display that collects measurements from slave units and presents numerical values and live charts on a graphical LCD.
problem: Make distributed industrial sensor readings available through a compact local display with configurable visual and numerical views.
approach: Collected sensor measurements through slave units and digital industrial connections.
Processed received data on an ATmega32-based master.
Built graphical and numerical views with physical navigation buttons.
outcome: A sensor-acquisition and display prototype with schematics, PCB work and multiple documented LCD interface states.

sections.title: From sensors to a local display
body: Sensor-connected slave units measure the required parameters and can perform initial processing. Data travels through digital connections and industrial ports to a master unit, where it is processed and displayed.

sections.title: An AVR master with two display modes
body: An ATmega32-based master receives the measurements and presents them on a 240 × 128 graphical LCD. Operators can switch between charts and numerical values.

sections.title: An interface built around physical controls
body: Buttons on the PCB navigate the main menu and settings. The interface includes a temperature chart, chart configuration and a warning view, shown in the original project photographs.

sections.title: Electronics and development tools
body: The project uses ATmega32A and ATmega8A microcontrollers, a single-layer PCB and a graphical LCD. Development used BASCOM AVR and Protel 99SE, bringing firmware, display logic and board work into one system.

strength: Distributed sensor data on a compact display.
contribution: My work covered embedded application and electronics development, including AVR display logic, schematic and PCB work for the sensor/slave/master prototype.
result: A sensor-acquisition and display prototype with schematics, PCB work and multiple documented LCD interface states.
decisionNotes: Sensor-connected slave units send measurements through digital connections to an ATmega32-based master. The 240 × 128 graphical LCD provides chart and numerical views, while physical PCB-mounted buttons navigate menus and settings.
validationNotes: The original schematic, single-layer PCB view and LCD photographs show the chart, temperature, menu, settings and warning states. These document the electronics and interface; no sensor-calibration, sampling-rate or measurement-accuracy study is supplied.
